title: Explicit finite tensor shifts and shift preservation of good complexes
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and a scheme W in the same universe, a flat-term K-flat complex P remains flat-term K-flat after every integer shift r [def-pod-completion-reindex-shifts]. Define the two finite comparisons on the direct-sum total tensor of reductions [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]: apply the ordinary reduction shift comparisons, then Mathlib’s first- or second-factor total tensor shift, then the scalar-restriction shift comparison. Define PodTensorFiniteShiftTransitions as the two adjacent quotient-square equations for these fixed maps, and PodTensorFiniteShiftGenerators as their homogeneous pure tensor formulas with coefficients 1 and (-1)^(p*r). No derived shift or witness of an existence theorem is chosen.

source.place: Steps 1 and 5; signed shifts of the same representative-normalized tensor operation. Supporting calculation: Stacks homology.tex, definition-shift-cochain, and more-algebra.tex, item-shift-tensor; descent: sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-pullback-tensor-product.

proof.text: The second-factor Mathlib total tensor shift identifies F tensor P[r] with (F tensor P)[r]. Acyclicity is stable under shifts and isomorphisms. Flatness of the shifted terms is the original term-flatness at i+r. Construct the two finite isomorphisms by functorial composition of the ordinary reduction shift, the native signed total tensor shift, and the ordinary scalar-restriction shift.
